title: Those Who Seem To Be Great
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 188
summary: This shabad opens with those who seem to be great and powerful. It turns the heart toward without the Lord's meditation, there is no salvation.
whyItMatters: It matters when life feels clingy, possessive, and afraid-to-lose because the shabad keeps attachment inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private momentum.
takeaway: Keep returning to this turn: without the Lord's meditation, there is no salvation.

lines.translation: Those who seem to be great and powerful,
are afflicted by the disease of anxiety. ||1||
Who is great by the greatness of Maya?

lines.gurmukhi: ਸੋ ਵਡਾ ਜਿਨਿ ਰਾਮ ਲਿਵ ਲਾਈ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: so vaddaa jin raam liv laiee ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: They alone are great, who are lovingly attached to the Lord. ||1||Pause||
The landlord fights over his land each day.
He shall have to leave it in the end, and yet his desire is still not satisfied. ||2||
Says Nanak, this is the essence of Truth:
without the Lord's meditation, there is no salvation. ||3||44||113||

structure: It opens by naming the condition without ornament: those who seem to be great and powerful.
The middle movement widens the correction through the landlord fights over his land each day.
It closes with a return you can actually keep: without the Lord's meditation, there is no salvation.
